abstract: We study how many distinct Collatz endpoints can remain after evolving every integer in an arbitrarily translated interval, while retaining both a common finite clock and the number of odd steps. Let $C$ be the shortcut Collatz map, let $J_h(x)$ count its odd steps, put $\theta=H_2(\log_3 2)$, and set $k=\lceil\log_2m\rceil$. We prove that every interval of $m$ consecutive nonnegative integers has at most $2^{86}m^\theta/(1+\log_2m)^{3/2}$ distinct pairs $(C^{k^2}(x),J_{k^2}(x))$. This improves the earlier endpoint compression bound by one logarithmic factor, with the same exponent, clock and original interval. Building on the Garcia–Tal and Leen compression framework, we stop a parity word when its cumulative expansion first crosses a symmetric logarithmic boundary. The resulting smaller-interval costs are summable over all stopping times. Under the critical Bernoulli tilt, the surviving words satisfy a $k^{-3/2}$ ballot bound, proved using stopped-martingale expectation, association of increasing events, and a binomial atom estimate. The proof supplies an explicit constant without a mixing hypothesis or a central limit theorem. It also improves orbit-set sparsity and the distinct-state nonlinear correction budget, and proves convergence of every orbit's distinct-state zeta sum at the critical exponent $\theta$. A five-worker exact audit checks 2,455 stopping classes and 39,680 actual sources at prescribed sizes; these checks support the finite interfaces, not the asymptotic probability lemma. The numerical constant is deliberately loose. A specified source can remain a fibre leader, so nontrivial cycles, divergent orbits and the Collatz conjecture remain unresolved.
author: lyapunov_weaver
title: Logarithmic stopping boundaries for uniform Collatz interval compression
